security_findings.finding: useEffect only depended on messages.length; a message content mutation (e.g. plan.securityStatus flipping approved/rejected) at the same array length would not re-trigger auto-scroll for a user at the bottom.
security_findings.fix: Replaced the [messages.length] dependency with a derived scrollTriggerKey covering message count + last message id + plan.securityStatus + text length, so in-place content changes on the last message also trigger auto-scroll-if-at-bottom. Dormant today (no in-place mutation exists yet) but closes the gap before it becomes a real bug once plan-status streaming lands.

security_findings.finding: Mount-time effect with isAtBottom=true default scrolls to bottom immediately when initialMessages is non-empty.
security_findings.note: This is the desired 'land at bottom of history' behavior for a chat app, not a defect.

security_findings.finding: handleScroll fires on every native scroll event without debounce/throttle.
security_findings.note: Cheap boolean setState, React bails on same-value updates; not a correctness issue at current scope.

security_findings.finding: The 'En yeni mesaja dön' button has no aria-live announcement when it appears — a screen-reader user scrolled away from bottom isn't told a new message arrived.
security_findings.note: Minor accessibility enhancement, not blocking; noted for a future a11y pass.

approved_points: 24px BOTTOM_THRESHOLD_PX + distanceFromBottom formula matches standard 'is user at bottom' pattern and AC-2 exactly.
scrollToBottom() falls back to direct scrollTop assignment when list.scrollTo is unavailable (jsdom), avoiding crashes in tests while using smooth scrollTo in real browsers.
'En yeni mesaja dön' button correctly unmounts (not just hides) when isAtBottom, keeping assertions unambiguous.
No conflict found between scroll state and isGeneratingPlan/editingPlanMessageId (Saga #264/#265) — fully independent.
77/77 tests green, diff matches code_diff.md/test_diff.md claims.
overall_assessment: Implementation satisfies all 5 ATDD acceptance criteria. One real medium-severity gap (length-only scroll trigger) fixed immediately with a low-cost content-aware key, since the task's own scenario explicitly anticipated plan-status changes. Three low-severity items accepted as out-of-scope polish.
